page: Amazon Web Services m8gb.12xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor architecture. It features 48 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, running at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. The server is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps. No local storage or dedicated GPU hardware is included in this configuration.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieves top-tier status in memory bandwidth tests, reaching 435.26 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations and 217.09 GB/sec for large-block write operations. Multi-core execution is highly efficient, as demonstrated by a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 24004.0 and strong stress-ng multi-core CPU performance. Database operations and static web serving throughput also rank in the top tier, with static web serving reaching 95.89 GB/sec.

While multi-core and memory throughput are excellent, single-core performance remains average, with Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core benchmarks falling into the middle 50 percent. Additionally, LLM text generation for small models is poor, though text generation for medium and large models performs in the top 25 percent. Given these characteristics, the m8gb.12xlarge is highly cost-efficient for multi-threaded workloads, software compilation, database management, and high-throughput web serving, while being less suited for single-threaded tasks or local storage-heavy applications.
